architecture.runtime_volume: The live ARaftSimWaterSurfaceActor remains the gameplay-water renderer and cooked-field consumer. Lava Canyon now binds a Chilko-local V2 instance of the shared transmitting water parent, with a cooked-field identity fallback for older maps and the same serialized instance in the regenerated runnable map.
architecture.runtime_detail: The retained Default Lit detail skin uses 0.035 calm and 0.14 active coverage. A first-party flow normal supplies sub-grid optical breakup, while a first-party foam-lace mask is multiplied by solver foam and speed and therefore cannot create whitewater in calm or dry cells.
architecture.capture_water: Filtered generation now creates a translucent Default Lit capture ribbon with physical IOR 1.333 and CPU-authored depth, bank-feather, and solver-aeration vertex opacity. The canonical landscape-candidate captures are technical evidence only and remain visibly below the target.
architecture.authority_boundary: The new textures, opacity, smoothing, optical coefficients, material instances, and capture shading are visual-only. Cooked depth, velocity, wet/dry state, bathymetry, coordinate mapping, live mesh topology, collision, buoyancy, raft forces, feature forcing, and rapid detection remain unchanged.

visual_comparison.method: Direct sRGB metrics over rows 260 through 719 of the identical 1280x720 breaking_water_side camera. Highlight fractions use normalized luminance thresholds 0.90 and 0.95.
visual_comparison.verdict: Retain as a bounded river-local optical improvement: V2 substantially reduces the broad chalk-white and extreme-highlight response, increases cold-water color separation, and replaces the prior regular glossy breakup with sparser solver-masked lace. The broad wave faces, sun reflection, shoreline, banks, and vegetation remain visibly procedural and sheet-like, so this is not photoreal acceptance.

remaining_photoreal_defects: The broad sun reflection and rapid highlights remain overexposed, with 3.38 percent of the measured water band above normalized luminance 0.90.
The large standing-wave faces remain too smooth and sheet-like and lack entrained-air depth, crest breakup, spray, mist, and rock-contact plumes.
The foam lace is a generated visual breakup mask rather than rapid-specific observed foam calibration, and only six rapid-foam vertices are active in the audited runtime state.
Bank geometry, shoreline contact, ground material, repeated vegetation silhouettes, rocks, atmosphere, and distance detail remain visibly procedural and blockout-quality.
The cooked Lava Canyon field remains unconverged and its discharge, bathymetry, stationing, hazards, and guide line are not calibrated to observed river behavior.
Raft, crew, equipment, animation, complete-run rescue and capsize behavior, packaged performance, and VR presentation still require final acceptance.
